claims.text_en: Sam Yot is an underground MRT Blue line station, code BL30, opened 29 July 2019 on the Hua Lamphong-Lak Song extension. Its box runs under Charoen Krung Road from Sam Yot junction (crossing with Mahachai Road) to Unakan junction; the ticket-hall buildings sit between Charoen Krung Rd and Soi Sam Yot, split by Soi Charoen Krung 5 and 7. The station's registered location spans khwaeng Wang Burapha Phirom and khwaeng Sanam Ratsadon (Sanam Chai), Phra Nakhon district, at 13.747250 N, 100.501333 E (app anchor 13.747, 100.5023 differs by roughly 90 m). Its planned name was Wang Burapha, changed to Sam Yot; published 2021 ridership was 1,758,892. The operator (BEM) and Wikipedia agree on the entrance buildings and the former name.

claims.text_en: The station itself and the historic Sam Yot / Wang Burapha quarter lie in Phra Nakhon district. Immediately east of the station, Khlong Ong Ang (the old city moat 'Khlong Rob Krung', dug 1783 under Rama I, registered as an ancient monument in 1976 by the Fine Arts Department) is an administrative boundary: the BMA Phra Nakhon district office states the canal 'is now the boundary between Phra Nakhon district and Samphanthawong district' for its restored stretch, while English Wikipedia places Saphan Lek (Damrong Sathit Bridge) on the boundary of Ban Bat subdistrict (Pom Prap Sattru Phai district, east/left bank) and Samphanthawong subdistrict (right bank). The Khlong Thom market / Mega Plaza / Saphan Lek toy blocks on the east bank are commonly addressed to Pom Prap subdistrict, Pom Prap Sattru Phai (DOPA 2025 lists that khwaeng at 11,795 residents). A 1.4 km2 catchment centred at Sam Yot junction plausibly touches all three khet — Phra Nakhon west of the canal, Pom Prap on the canal's north-east bank, Samphanthawong at the south-east (Saphan Han / Chakkrawat) fringe. The exact Voronoi polygon is not independently verifiable from public sources; the split between Pom Prap (upper canal) and Samphanthawong (lower canal) sections is a researcher reading of two official boundary statements.

claims.text_en: Computed as coordinate deltas from the station's published position (approx 111 km per degree latitude; no Overpass available): Blue line neighbours Sanam Chai (BL29) approx 0.6-0.7 km southwest and Wat Mangkon (BL31) approx 0.9-1.0 km southeast — both beyond the 800 m cap centre-to-centre, so their Voronoi cells clip this unit's southern and south-eastern edges, consistent with the app. To the east there is no rail stop within 800 m; MRT Phetchaburi on Phetchaburi Road sits roughly 4-5 km east and ARL Ratchaprarop roughly 3.5-4 km east — neither bounds this unit (the east side runs into the old-town blocks and Khlong Maha Nak direction, then Hua Lamphong's cell approx 1.5 km southeast). The Giant Swing / Wat Suthat at Sao Chingcha is approx 0.35-0.6 km northeast (inside; a Thai travel guide gives 600 m from Exit 3). Wat Ratchanatdaram / Loha Prasat is approx 0.7-0.75 km north-northeast — at the unit's fringe, which plausibly explains the conflicting unit attribution noted in batch 2 (its street address is given as Mahachai Road, Bang Khun Phrom, Phra Nakhon). Democracy Monument is approx 1.1 km north — outside the 800 m unit. Rattanakosin Exhibition Hall approx 0.85-0.9 km north — outside/at the edge.

claims.text_en: The name comes from a Grand Palace outer gate. A wooden gate (Phueat Thibat, ประตูพฤฒิบาศ) stood there from Rama I's reign; under Rama V it was replaced by a cement gate with three gateways, each topped by a spire — hence 'Sam Yot', literally three peaks. Italian engineer Carlo Allegri advised demolition as traffic grew; demolition began in the second half of 1897. In its heyday the area was an amphoe (district) of Phra Nakhon province, hosted the legal lottery house (โรงหวย ก ข) and foreign department stores (B Grimm at the intersection's south-east corner); it was downgraded to a tambon under Rama VII. A 2025 university walking-tour brief states the gate stood at today's MRT Sam Yot Exit 1 forecourt. The quarter's arc is documented as the 'Sam Yot-Wang Burapha-Phahurat' commercial district of the 4th-6th reigns (Museum Siam touring exhibition; M2F). This is the identity backbone for vibe 10.

claims.text_en: Blue line entrances: Building 1 on Mahachai Road at Sam Yot junction (facing Rommaninat Park and the Corrections Museum; escalator), Building 2 at Soi Charoen Krung 5/7 (lift only), Building 3 on the Burapha/Unakan side (escalator) for Wat Suthat, Old Siam Plaza, Sao Chingcha and the City Hall direction — the entrance cluster is on the Charoen Krung/Mahachai side, not on Dinso Road. Service per Thai Wikipedia: toward Lak Song first train 05:52 (Mon-Fri) / 06:01 (weekends-holidays), last 00:12; toward Tha Phra last 23:26 (weekdays). Buses from the adjacent stops: 1, 8, 25, 35, 43, 48, 53 (loop), 73, 507, 508 and others on Charoen Krung and Mahachai roads; moto-taxi connections. No BTS line reaches the old town. The Purple line southern extension will make Sam Yot interchange PP23, with four listed future exits (Thonon Luang Rd; Suan Sam Yot park / Saphan Damrong Sathit / Vachiratham 72 arch; Soi Sirichai / Rommaninat Park; Sam Yot connecting to the Blue line). Transport 7 is coherent: heavy MRT + bus coverage, no BTS, entrances offset from the Dinso side.

claims.text_en: The character claims: station architecture in Rama V-era / Chino-Portuguese style echoing the old gate (operator and travel press); a protected historic quarter — the canal frontage is a Fine Arts Department registered ancient monument and the area carries a building-tone control law keeping facades white-cream (a 2025 interior-design feature on a canal-side cafe conversion states this directly). Everyday texture: old restaurants from residents' childhoods still trading alongside newer openings, 'several good bars' nearby, walkable to both Yaowarat and Rattanakosin, in a resident-family's account (ReadtheCloud, 2025-12-19). Adaptive reuse is visible: a 50-year-old farm-machinery warehouse on Mahachai Road 775 became Piccolo Vicolo cafe plus a fourth-floor guest suite (2025 articles), and Hotel Kcha/Kacha occupies a former princely residence opposite the station. The quarter's identity story ('Sam Yot-Wang Burapha-Phahurat', 4th-6th reign modernisation) is curated in a Museum Siam exhibition. Vibe 10 reads as identity/heritage-based rather than commerce-based.

claims.text_en: Official schedule: BMA's district-office page and TAT describe Khlong Ong Ang Walking Street every Friday-Sunday 16:00-22:00 along 1.5 km of both banks (Damrong Sathit to Saphan Han/Bophit Phimukh bridges), with free 30-minute kayak sessions (last queue 20:00) from the Phra Nakhon bank near Saphan Lek Square, street art, live music. Counter-view: a 2024-08-26 Thairath feature reports the canal area stagnant after COVID — a vendor compared the current year to last as far worse ('now it is like being in the ICU'), proposed shrinking the market to Sat-Sun 13:00-19:00, and activity has survived mainly through occasional government festivals (BMA/TAT 'Walking Street Food ONG ANG CANAL', 8-12 Aug 2024, 12:00-22:00, Saphan Han to Saphan Bophit Phimukh). Wongnai user reviews dated 2025-03-22 and 2025-09-11 similarly describe quiet daytime, few shops open, and kayak/live-music activities suspended at times, while praising evening walks and murals. In 2026 the area anchored a free four-canal 'Rattanakosin Walk Market' (24-31 July 2026, 09:00-21:30, Time Out Bangkok). Verdict: vibe 10 is defensible for identity and event evenings; ordinary weekday evenings are thin.

claims.text_en: The Democracy Monument at Ratchadamnoen Klang x Dinso Road is Bangkok's default assembly point, and Dinso Road itself is repeatedly named in police traffic advisories around rallies (e.g., 19 July 2023 protest of roughly 300 people at the monument, with closures on Ratchadamnoen Klang and Dinso; a 2 Aug 2025 patriotic rally also gathered there; in Nov 2021 police fenced the circle entirely). A May-1992 memorial park on Ratchadamnoen had a public-park build-out planned with BMA funding in 2568 (2025) per a Taejai crowdfunding page (fundraising window 13 Aug 2024 - 31 Dec 2025). Measured from the station the monument is approx 1.1 km north — outside the 800 m unit — so rally energy reaches this catchment only as occasional road closures at the northern fringe (Ratchadamnoen/Dinso), not as a unit-level crowd or venue. Editors should not credit event vibrancy to this unit on the monument's account.

claims.text_en: Neither English nor Thai searches surfaced crime statistics, incident reporting or resident-safety discourse specific to the Sam Yot catchment. What exists is generic and district-level: travel-guide genre notes that old-town backstreets empty and dim after roughly 22:00 and that the main reported risks around Bangkok's old-town tourist zones are scams, overcharging and pickpocketing rather than violent crime (snippet-level only); Chinatown/Khao San tourist-fringe spillover is the usual concern in the genre. Counter-evidence: the unit hosts government offices (BMA City Hall approx 0.45 km north), a patrolled public park with facilities until 21:00, an MRT station with staffed entrances, and 2025 user reviews describe relaxed evening walks on the canal without safety complaints. Nothing unit-specific supports a 5; nothing justifies raising it either — the basis looks generic (old-town night emptiness, tourist-zone friction). Treat safety 5 as unexplained by current evidence.

claims.text_en: Rommaninat Park (Mahachai Road, facing Exit 1) occupies the former Bangkok Prison (Klong Prem Central Prison's original site; the prison moved to Chatuchak in 1972-era relocations). Bangkok's BMA green-spaces portal lists it as 'Suan Romanee Nat' with free admission, daily hours of roughly 04:00/05:00-21:00; retained prison walls and guard towers survive inside; facilities include an outdoor fitness area with machines and free weights, children's playground, skatepark and basketball court; the small Corrections Museum on its edge opens Thursday-Saturday. The second green asset is the Khlong Ong Ang promenade: 750 m along both banks (1,500 m total, renovated 2018-2019 per BMA), walkable at any time (the Fri-Sun market is an overlay, not a gate), kayak sessions on weekends. The Purple line exit list also names a small Suan Sam Yot park near Saphan Damrong Sathit. Green 9 in a 1.4 km2 unit rests on this park-plus-promenade combination; caveat: the app's 4.4 ha park figure could not be independently confirmed because the BMA park page returned HTTP 403 — hours and facilities are corroborated across TAT and other pages, the area figure remains app-only.

claims.text_en: The housing is overwhelmingly old shophouse fabric and small low-rise apartment stock rather than new condos: Rattanakosin conservation rules (including the white-cream tone-control law on the canal frontage) constrain redevelopment, and quoted renovation cases work with 50-year-old buildings kept 'as found'. The resident base is shrinking — registered population of khwaeng Wang Burapha Phirom fell from 10,414 (2019 DOPA) to 8,344 (BMA, 4 Feb 2025) and 8,238 (DOPA 2568 release), with khet Phra Nakhon overall at 39,264 people over 5.536 km2. Meanwhile tourism demand converts stock: guesthouses on Thani Road at 650-1,250 THB/night, canal-side cafe/Airbnb conversions (2025), hostels by the station. Condition stories: the as-is 20-year-tenant shophouse listing and the 1970s-warehouse conversion both show aging but salvageable fabric; no wholesale renewal scheme for this catchment surfaced — change happens building by building.

Daily-essentials 9 is supported by market density; the hospital gap is the one soft spot.

claims.text_en: A 2025 Urban Ally study of the Sam Yot station area (input to BMA's Bangkok pedestrian-bicycle master plan, plan horizon 2567-2575 BE = 2024-2032, study radius 2 km from the station) describes a small-block grid crossed by parallel spines with Tanao Road as the connecting spine and Sam Yot station at the Charoen Krung x Mahachai crossing; it flags the walkability problem that several roads (Tanao, Dinso, Charoen Krung, Tri Phet) carry both collector and access traffic, that road space is allocated to cars, and that some narrow secondary roads lack footways. Short-term pilots chosen: a cycle lane on Siriphong Road and a pedestrian-priority treatment of the road in front of BMA City Hall, explicitly 'to make the Sam Yot station to Dinso Road link safer' — the north pilot line runs approx 1.8 km from the station toward Ratchadamnoen, the south line approx 1.7 km to Saphan Phut pier (13 links, 10 junctions in the 3.5 km package). Earlier (2020), a BMA 'araya-pat' pilot upgraded the footway route from Sam Yot station along the canal to Chao Phraya Sky Park. MRT entrance buildings stand on the Charoen Krung/Mahachai side; reaching Dinso Road means crossing heavy-traffic blocks — consistent with transport 7 rather than higher.

claims.text_en: (1) MRT Purple line southern extension (Tao Poon-Rat Burana): construction from Aug 2022; Sam Yot is one of two underground stations in Contract 3 (3.12 km twin bore); progress reported 53.4% in Apr 2025 and approx 79.4% in an Oct 2026 Nation Thailand report, with the full extension targeted for November 2030 — later than earlier 2027/2028 talk. Until then Mahachai Road in front of Rommaninat Park carries construction sites; the future Purple exits will land at Suan Sam Yot, Saphan Damrong Sathit / the Vachiratham 72 arch, Soi Sirichai and Rommaninat Park. (2) BMA canal programme: at a late-Nov 2025 meeting, walkway connections at Saphan Ong Uthit and under Sanam Sae road were due mid-December 2025, 8 app-bookable water taxis planned, and a walkway under Phan Fa Lilat bridge agreed with MRTA (completion ~2570) — Bangkok Biznews, 2025-11-27; treat 'mid-Dec 2025' items as reported plans, not verified completions. (3) 2026 programming: the free four-canal Rattanakosin Walk Market (24-31 July 2026) put traders back along Khlong Ong Ang. (4) Private-side recovery: cafe/guesthouse conversions and widened Thipsamai hours (2024-2025). Nothing found indicating a wholesale redevelopment of the shophouse fabric; change is incremental.

question_answers.notes: Underground Blue-line station BL30 (opened 29 Jul 2019) beneath Charoen Krung Rd at the Sam Yot junction, in the Wang Burapha quarter of Phra Nakhon; the catchment straddles the Khlong Ong Ang canal which is itself a khet boundary (Phra Nakhon west; Pom Prap on the NE bank at Khlong Thom/Mega Plaza; Samphanthawong at the Saphan Han/Chakkrawat fringe). Clipped by Sanam Chai (SW) and Wat Mangkon (SE); no rail stop east within 800 m (st.phetchaburi and st.ratchaprarop do NOT bound this unit); Democracy Monument ~1.1 km N is outside; Giant Swing ~350-600 m NE is inside; Wat Ratchanatdaram sits on the northern fringe.

A government-office quarter (City Hall ~0.45 km N) of aging shophouses and small low-rise apartments in a tone-controlled conservation zone, with a shrinking registered population and a tourist/service edge at markets and the canal. No unit-specific safety evidence was found; safety 5 appears to reflect generic old-town night emptiness and tourist-fringe friction (scams/pickpocketing genre) rather than any documented local driver — flagged unresolved.

Transport 7: strong MRT+buses but no BTS and entrances offset from the Dinso side; walkability flagged as car-priority on key streets. Rent 8: real small-unit asks 11,000-15,000 THB near the station against a 13,500/27,000 blend. Essentials/food 9: dawn markets (Trok Mo, Khlong Thom) plus market malls and 553 food venues with named famous anchors. Green 9: Rommaninat Park (free, to 21:00) plus the always-open 750-m-per-bank canal promenade. Mechanisms documented in c05, c10, c11, c13, c14.

Both are true in part: official Fri-Sun 16:00-22:00 walking street and 2024-2026 festival programming vs 2024 vendor accounts of post-COVID stagnation ('like being in the ICU'), suspended kayak/music at times, and quiet daytime (2025 reviews). Weekday evenings are thin; event nights are the exception. Old-building conditions show aging but salvageable stock (20-year-tenant as-is shophouse, 50-year warehouse conversions); no wholesale decay story. Heat: only generic guidance found (evening hours preferred for the canal walk) — no unit-specific claim.

Evening life = Fri-Sun canal walking street (unstable operation), occasional government festivals, small bars (rooftops and standing bars around Sao Chingcha/Wang Burapha), the Chinatown dining gravity next door, and rally days ~1.1 km north at Democracy Monument (outside this unit; effect limited to occasional Dinso/Ratchadamnoen closures). Vibe 10 is identity- and event-driven, not steady street life.

Rommaninat Park: free, daily roughly 04:00/05:00-21:00 (sources differ on opening by an hour), facilities incl. fitness, skatepark, basketball; prison walls retained; museum Thu-Sat. Khlong Ong Ang: promenade open at all times (market is an overlay Fri-Sun 16:00-22:00 per BMA/TAT; kayak last queue 20:00). Caveat: BMA park page 403 — the app's 4.4 ha figure remains unverified.

In-catchment listings: studios 11,000-13,000 THB 74-100 m from the station; 1BR condos 14,000-15,000; old shophouse 20,000; whole shophouses 45,000+. Blend 13,500/27,000 matches the small-unit market; conservation rules keep new supply out; resident population shrinking while tourist conversions take some stock.

Wet markets at dawn (Trok Mo 05:00-10:00; Khlong Thom fresh zone 05:00-09:00), retail malls at both exits (Mega Plaza, China World, Old Siam, Phahurat), clinics on Dinso/Mahachai; no verified general or 24-hour hospital inside the unit — nearest public general hospitals 2-4 km (researcher estimate).

Small bars, not a club district: Swing Bar by Ching Cha (rooftop), Tai Soon Bar, Foxhole BKK, Motu, Qasbar etc. in the Sao Chingcha/Wang Burapha pocket; the heavy nightlife (Soi Nana craft bars, Yaowarat cocktail rooms) belongs to Wat Mangkon's unit and Khao San to others. Recommend the editorial note state the 9 rests on proximity to both nightlife districts.

Entrance buildings on the Charoen Krung/Mahachai side (Building 1 at Sam Yot junction facing Rommaninat; Building 2 lift-only; Building 3 toward Burapha/Unakan). Dinso Rd carries collector-plus-access traffic with car-priority space allocation (Urban Ally 2025); pilots planned to link station-Dinso on foot/bike (Siriphong Rd cycle lane, City Hall-front pedestrian street). Canal promenade runs 750 m per bank, ~100-300 m from the station. Distances stated throughout; no walking durations derived.

Weekday: office/government rhythm around City Hall, dawn markets, thin evenings. Fri-Sun: canal walking street overlay (when operating). Annual/civic: rally days at Democracy Monument (outside unit, closure spillover), Loy Krathong and 2026 four-canal market events, MRT service to ~00:12-00:30.

Purple line works toward a Nov 2030 interchange (construction disruption on Mahachai Rd until then); BMA canal walkway/water-taxi programme (reported plan, Dec 2025); 2026 four-canal market; incremental cafe/guesthouse conversions amid a shrinking resident base; outside-the-score: rally closures, conservation constraints on supply, no hospital in unit, unverified park area.

preview.text_en: A three-khet heritage stop on Dinso Road: the always-open Khlong Ong Ang promenade at the door, 11,000-THB studios two minutes' walk from it, and Rommaninat Park across the boundary.

guide_lead.text_en: Sam Yot is the old town's quiet rail corner — an underground Blue-line station beneath Charoen Krung at the Sam Yot junction, straddling Phra Nakhon, Pom Prap Sattru Phai and Samphanthawong. The Khlong Ong Ang promenade (Friday-Sunday walking street, kayaks, street art) runs beside the station, and listings put 11,000-13,000 THB studios and 14,000-15,000 THB 1-bedrooms at the door. The trade-offs: safety 5 has no visible unit-specific basis, evening life is event-driven rather than street-level, and the district's registered population is shrinking. Purple Line interchange targeted November 2030.

strengths.text_en: Khlong Ong Ang promenade — restored moat canal, verified inside the catchment — gives daily waterside walking plus a Fri-Sun 16:00-22:00 walking street.
Rent 8 is backed by hard listings: 11,000-13,000 THB studios 74-100 m from the station and 14,000-15,000 THB 1-bedrooms.
Market density (Trok Mo dawn market, Khlong Thom, Mega Plaza) supports daily_essentials 9 for a car-free household.

tradeoffs.text_en: Safety 5 has no visible unit-specific evidence base — only generic old-town night emptiness after ~22:00 and the tourist-fringe scam genre.
Vibe 10 / nightlife 9 are event- and heritage-driven: the 17 small bars and the Fri-Sun walking street carry it, and the canal's revival has stagnated between festivals.

day_night.text_en: Daytime is a government-office and market quarter; evenings depend on the Fri-Sun walking street and small bars, with backstreets dim after ~22:00.

within_area_variation.text_en: The station quarter (Wang Burapha, Dinso) differs from the canal-frontage blocks and from the Pom Prap and Samphanthawong fringes the catchment touches.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: heritage-oriented renters on a budget who walk and use the canal promenade as their green.
Poor fit: park-dependent households — Rommaninat Park computes outside the catchment (st.sanam-chai side) despite facing Exit 1.

uncertainties: safety 5: No unit-specific evidence for the 5 was found in EN or TH sources; keep the rating but pair it with an explicit 'basis: generic old-town night emptiness + tourist-friction genre; nothing local documented' note. The quarter has a staffed MRT station, government offices and a park open to 21:00 — a plain safety deficit is not evidenced. Recommend the app label this rating low-confidence for this unit.

vibe 10 + nightlife 9 with 17 venues: Vibe 10 is defensible as heritage identity (three-peaked-gate story, tone-controlled streets, adaptive reuse) plus event evenings; nightlife 9 with 17 mapped venues only makes sense as small in-unit bars plus immediate access to Chinatown's Soi Nana and the old-town tourist edge. State that mechanism explicitly; do not imply a club district.

green 9: Supported by Rommaninat Park (free, to ~21:00, fitness/skate/basketball) and the always-open canal promenade; caveat that the 4.4 ha park figure is app-only (BMA page 403) and walking-street operation on the canal is intermittent — the promenade, not the market, is the dependable green asset. | Coordinator correction 2026-11-07: Rommaninat Park computes OUTSIDE the catchment polygon (st.sanam-chai side); the in-unit green case rests on Khlong Ong Ang, temple and institutional grounds.

rent 8: Listings corroborate the blend: 11,000-13,000 THB studios steps from the station, 14,000-15,000 THB 1BR condos, 20,000 THB aged shophouse; whole-shophouse asks are much higher, so 'cheap' applies to rooms and small units. Portal asks, not transacted rents.

daily_essentials 9: Market density is real (dawn wet markets, market malls, 553 food venues); the soft spot is hospitals — none verified inside the unit, nearest general hospitals several km. Consider reflecting that in the essentials narrative rather than the score.

crowd 2 / transport 7: Crowd 2 matches shrinking registered population (Wang Burapha 10,414 to 8,344, 2019-2025) and a daytime-office swell pattern. Transport 7 matches MRT+bus strength, no BTS, and car-priority streets between station and Dinso (2025 pilot programme exists).
